newsitem.title: USA: HP says cleared to market InkJet cartridges.
newsitem.headline: HP says cleared to market InkJet cartridges.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Monday a ruling by a federal judge allows it to continue marketing a new version of popular inkjet printer cartridges designed to be more reliable than earlier versions.

However, Hewlett-Packard said U.S. District Judge James Ware's ruling, handed down late Friday, found the packaging now being used on its old-style cartridges, which it continues to manufacture, falsely depicts the new cartridges on the outside.
The judge is expected to spell out the terms related to the packaging of HP's old-style cartridges at a hearing set for July 23.

The rulings follow litigation brought by Dallas-based Nu-Kote International Inc., which markets ink that can be injected into the older-style HP cartridges and had asked the court to stop HP from making the new InkJet cartridges.

Nu-Kote had argued that the new cartridges unfairly restrict competition. The new products eliminate a hole on top of the cartridge which Nu-Kote and other makers of replacement ink used to enable customers to inject the ink.

Jeremy James, a spokesman for HP's consumer products group based in San Diego, said the judge had ruled against a major part of Nu-Kote's motion, but found the new packaging on older-style cartridges constituted false labeling.

"The judge said we can continue to manufacture the (new) bottom-ink-filled cartridges, which is the far more substantive issue," James said. It will take up to 18 months to complete changeover of manufacturing to the new design.

"We need to await the judge's specific terms on the packaging injunction," he said. "However, our belief at this time is should the judge require us to produce new packaging for the top-filled cartridges, the cost will not have a material impact on HP's finances."
James said HP managers had estimated the cost that could be incurred in rectifying the packaging of older-style cartridges would be in the $3 million to $6 million range.
Nu-Kote said in a statement issued Sunday that Judge Ware had ruled the packaging to be "literally false" in incorrectly depicting the cartridges it contains.

Nu-Kote's motion for an injunction is part of litigation between the two companies. Hewlett-Packard originally sued Nu-Kote for patent infringement, and Nu-Kote filed a counterclaim on antitrust grounds.

Hewlett-Packard said it had redesigned the cartridges, including popular cartridges used in some DeskJet printers and OfficeJet multifunction and fax machines, to improve reliability by moving the fill hole to the bottom.
